newsitem.title: USA: Warren Buffett says most stocks overvalued - paper.
newsitem.headline: Warren Buffett says most stocks overvalued - paper.

text.p: Warren Buffet said in his annual letter to shareholders of Berkshire Hathaway Inc, the company he chairs, that he believed most stocks were overvalued, the New York Times reported on Monday.

"The overpayment risk surfaces periodically and, in our opinion, may now be quite high for the purchasers of nearly all stocks," he was quoted by the New York Times as saying in a letter to shareholders.

Buffett was quoted in the paper as saying: "Investors making purchases in an overheated market need to recognize that it may often take an extended period for the value of even an outstanding company to catch up with the price they paid."
The paper said Buffett indicated that while some stocks Berkshire held might be considered overvalued, he had no intention of selling them.
The annual report also disclosed Berkshire owned 30.2 million McDonald's Corp shares, up from the 9.34 million shares owned at the end of September 1995, the paper said.
